title: Euler product of the $L$-function of a lisse sheaf
statement:
Let $U_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, let
$U=U_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G_0$ be a lisse
Weil sheaf on $U_0$. Then, as
power series in $t$ (the Euler series of [d-real-cohom]),

$$
\prod_{x\in|U_0|}\det\bigl(1-F_xt^{d(x)},\mathcal G_{0,\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}
=
\frac{\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(U,\mathcal G))}
{\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(U,\mathcal G))},
$$

where $|U_0|$ is the set of closed points, $d(x)$ the degree of
$x$, and the right-hand side is the graded form of the
Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] of the trace-formula chapter (summed
with the signs $(-1)^{i+1}$).

proof.text: *Finite-level hypotheses.* By [def-wf-weil-category], $\mathcal G_0$ is an object $(E,(G_E,\varphi))$ of $\mathrm{WeilD}(U_0,\Qlb)$: $E/\Ql$ is finite in $\Qlb$, $G_E$ lies in $\mathcal C_E=D^b_c(U,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and $\varphi:P_EG_E\xrightarrow{\sim}G_E$. This is the representative $(E,K_E)$ required in [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar]. The objects of $D^b_c(U,E)$ are those of the integral category $D^b_c(U,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] ($U$ is of finite type over $k$, hence noetherian of finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible on it), so $K_{\mathcal O}=G_E$ with $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ is a lattice as in [thm-trf-trace-formula-e]. Membership of $G_E$ in that integral category includes compatible pairs $(L_n,\alpha_n)$ with $L_n\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A_{E,n})$ and $\alpha_n:\nu_U^*L_n\xrightarrow{\sim}G_E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$; each is an explicit etale-origin witness of the reduction $K_n$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], and these are retained. For admissibility: $U_0$ is affine, hence separated, and of finite type over $k_0$, a curve in the sense of [d-real-setup]; by [thm-nagata-compactification] the separated finite-type morphism $U_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ to the quasi-compact quasi-separated base has a compactification over $k_0$, which we fix. The graph correspondences of the iterates $\Phi^m$ and the fixed-point base changes on its base change to $k$ are separated finite-type morphisms between finite-type $k$-schemes with separated targets (products, compactifications and closed fixed loci of separated schemes). By [def-trf-admissibility] the exceptional-adjoint datum is a theorem for every such morphism, with adjunction and compactification comparisons from [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and stage-independent bounds from [thm-sf-preservation-class]. Thus every finite-level hypothesis of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] holds for this lattice, and so do the hypotheses of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] for $\mathcal G_0$.

Apply the curve case of the Euler-product form of the trace formula
[thm-trf-l-function-euler-product] with $\Lambda=\Qlb$,
$X_0=U_0$ (separated of finite type, of dimension one, by [d-real-setup]) and
$K=\mathcal G_0$, a sheaf placed in degree zero; its hypotheses are those
of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar], verified in Step 1. Its local factor at a
closed point $x$ is $\det(1-t^{e_x}F^{\mathrm{trf}}_x\mid\mathcal G_{0,\bar x})$
with $e_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]=d(x)$ and $F^{\mathrm{trf}}_x$ its one-circuit local
Frobenius: the scalar extension to $\Qlb$ of the $E$-stage operator $F_{y,e_x}$
of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] for a representative and a lattice
with finite-Tor reductions, $y$ a rational point under $x$. The $F_x$ of the
statement is the local geometric Frobenius of [def-weil-punctual-weights], i.e. the
operator of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] on the same stalk.
By [lem-rp-local-frobenius-models-agree] the two operators are conjugate on every
$\mathcal H^j(\mathcal G_0)_{\bar x}$ (only $j=0$ occurs), so the two local
determinants agree, and they do not depend on the choices of $\bar x$ by
[lem-weil-local-frobenius-conjugacy-class]. Hence the $L(U_0,\mathcal G_0,t)$ of
[thm-trf-l-function-euler-product] is the left-hand side, and its items (2) and (3) give

$$
\frac{\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(U,\mathcal G))}
{\det(1-Ft,H_c^0(U,\mathcal G))\,\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(U,\mathcal G))},
$$

with $F$ and $H_c^i$ those of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar], as the statement specifies.

Finally $H_c^0(U,\mathcal G)=0$ by [lem-a1-affine-hc0], whose hypotheses (a smooth geometrically connected affine curve and a lisse Weil sheaf on it) are those of the statement. Its compact support cohomology is that of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], built on the same rational compact-support functor whose scalar extension to $\Qlb$ is the $H_c^0$ of Step 2. So the factor $i=0$ is the determinant of $1-Ft$ on the zero space, namely $1$, and Step 2 gives the displayed identity.
